areas.summary: Limited public evidence for curriculum (1 excerpt; mostly general statements rather than specific provision).

signals.text: Embed an ambitious and representative curriculum that enables pupils to understand, respect and celebrate diversity, challenge stereotypes and prepare for life in modern Britain.
signals.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - Equality and Diversity

areas.narrativeSummary: Embed an ambitious and representative curriculum that enables pupils to understand, respect and celebrate diversity, challenge stereotypes and prepare for life in modern Britain.

areas.summary: Strong publicly visible evidence for enrichment and extra-curricular activity (8 specific items). Listed provision includes rugby, dance, tag rugby, after-school club, after school club, holiday club, physical education. 1 item corroborated across multiple pages.

signals.text: Past clubs have included Baking, Dance, Tag Rugby, Rounders, Newspaper Club, Craft, Outside Games & Adventure Clubs run for approximately 5-7 weeks and there is a charge of £1.00 per session to cover expenses.
signals.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - After School Clubs

signals.text: Within this approach, the use of natural materials and loose parts are used, encouraging children to explore, investigate and learn through first-hand experiences of open-ended resources, providing them with endless opportunities to be curious, sparking their imagination and creating wow moments of awe and wonder!
signals.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - Welcome to Reception

signals.text: Winslow Church of England School After School Clubs After School Clubs Each term we offer teacher led after-school clubs.
signals.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - After School Clubs

signals.text: The School Games Mark is a Government-led award scheme launched in 2012, facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust to reward schools for their commitment to the development of competition across their school and into the community, and we are delighted to have been recognised for our success.
signals.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - PE & Sports Premium

areas.narrativeSummary: The school website lists rugby, dance, tag rugby, after-school club, after school club, holiday club and 1 more. Information appears across 3 pages.

areas.summary: Moderate publicly visible evidence for ethos and values (3 specific items). Listed provision includes formal pshe lessons.

signals.text: It is underpinned by our Christian , values – kindness, forgiveness, honesty, respect and love to learn – and Jesus’ teaching of shining our light before others and giving glory to God.
signals.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - Collective Worship & Spirituality

signals.text: But communication is more than just words and through informal discussion, Collective Worship and formal PSHE lessons, all pupils understand the school’s high expectations of their behaviour, showing respect to all the community.
signals.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - Curriculum

signals.text: Children leave Winslow Church of England School with a sense of belonging to a close-knit, caring community, self-belief and a recognition of how they might be a force for change in the wider world.

Key Info
PE & Sports Premium
PE & Sports Premium
Winslow Church of England School receives a Sports Premium which enables us to enhance the opportunities and resources we provide in Physical Education for pupils at our school. We use this funding to offer participation in sports festivals, bespoke coaching, and provision of equipment. Please click below to see how we allocate our sports funding.
We are delighted to announce that Winslow CE School, have achieved the School Games Gold Mark Award for our commitment and engagement in the School Games for the 2025/26 academic year.
The School Games Mark is a Government-led award scheme launched in 2012, facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust to reward schools for their commitment to the development of competition across their school and into the community, and we are delighted to have been recognised for our success.

Winslow Church of England School
About our School
Governors
The role of the Governing Board is to act as a critical friend to the school and to ensure that it carries out its statutory responsibilities. The Governing Board is responsible for setting the school budget, approving policies, monitoring performance, and along with the Head Teacher, for setting the strategic direction of the school and raising standards of achievement.
Governors are appointed by the Local Authority and by the Church (Foundation Governors) and can also be members of the local community. A number of staff and parents are elected onto the Governing Body for a period of four years service, after which time they can stand for re-election.

Alternatively, you may write to the Governing Board via the school office, marking it for the attention of the Chair of Governors and labelled ‘confidential’.

Welcome to Reception
Within our Early Years Reception Provision, we have two classes; Sky Class and Sunshine Class. Whilst we have separate classes, we work very closely together and share both an indoor and continuous outdoor provision environment. We have very recently implemented 'The Hygge Approach' to enable a calm, nurturing environment which fosters feelings of cosiness, happiness and familiarity, capturing a sense of security and wellbeing for children during their early stages of education. Within this approach, the use of natural materials and loose parts are used, encouraging children to explore, investigate and learn through first-hand experiences of open-ended resources, providing them with endless opportunities to be curious, sparking their imagination and creating wow moments of awe and wonder!

pageCache.pageTitle: Winslow Church of England School - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Winslow Church of England School
Curriculum
Curriculum Intent and Implementation Plan
Our vision is ‘Let your light shine’. The rainbow symbolises God’s unconditional love for each individual. We seek to reflect that light in all we do: in our community, both local and wider, our communication, both word and action, with curiosity and courage, and with care and compassion for everyone, inspiring a love of learning. This Christian vision drives and shapes all we do, including our curriculum.
Every child and adult is recognised as a unique individual, with their own particular gifts to share within our loving and inclusive school community. However, we also strive to keep looking outwards, understanding and appreciating our place in the local and global community. Each child is helped to achieve their full potential, regardless of their background, so that they are equipped to take their place in an increasingly diverse world.
Clear communication is vital. We recognise how important it is for all our children to build a rich vocabulary, to help them comprehend what they read and also bring their writing to life across the curriculum. Having built the confidence of our youngest pupils through phonics, each child is introduced to the wonderful world of reading. They are exposed to high quality texts, testing their skills of decoding and comprehension through ‘Accelerated Reader’ quizzes and learning to think like an author, as they explore language and intent through regular ‘Book Talk’ sessions. But communication is more than just words and through informal discussion, Collective Worship and formal PSHE lessons, all pupils understand the school’s high expectations of their behaviour, showing respect to all the community.
Curiosity and Courage
At Winslow Church of England School, we help each child learn to value themselves, but also to appreciate difference. Coming from diverse backgrounds, we help every pupil develop the positive attitudes and life skills needed throughout their life. Within a safe learning environment, teachers seek to cultivate skills such as personal resilience, perseverance and team work, the ‘growth mind-set’ needed to promote responsibility for learning and future success. Children leave Winslow Church of England School with a sense of belonging to a close-knit, caring community, self-belief and a recognition of how they might be a force for change in the wider world.
At the heart of our life together in school is a desire for all our pupils to become compassionate and caring towards those around them. We recognise that children need to be in the right ‘head-space’ to access their learning, and so we provide the necessary support to help all pupils make the right choices. Pupils understand that some of their friends struggle with behaviour and need extra help and care to overcome difficulties. Year 6 pupils are trained as peer mentors and some pupils are paired with an adult mentor, providing a ‘go to person’ with whom anxieties can be shared.

Equality and Diversity
Equality and Diversity
Winslow Church of England School demonstrates a strong culture of inclusion through our vision, values and culture of the school.
Staff and Governors are committed to promoting equality of opportunity across the school community and take seriously the requirements of the Public Sector Equality Duty as defined by section 149 of the Equality Act 2010.
In summary, those subject to the general equality duty must have due regard to the need to:
Equality Objectives for 2026 - 2028:
Ensure every pupil experiences an inclusive school culture where diversity is valued, protected and actively promoted, and where all pupils feel they belong regardless of protected characteristic or background.
Embed an ambitious and representative curriculum that enables pupils to understand, respect and celebrate diversity, challenge stereotypes and prepare for life in modern Britain.
Improve outcomes for disadvantaged and vulnerable pupils by identifying and removing barriers to learning, ensuring equitable access to high-quality teaching and the wider curriculum.
Promote positive representation by ensuring pupils encounter diverse role models, experiences and perspectives that broaden aspirations and challenge stereotypes.
Develop pupils' understanding of local, national and global communities so they value difference, show empathy and contribute positively to society.
Eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation
Advance equality of opportunity between different groups
Foster good relations between different groups

Winslow Church of England School
Junior Road Safety Officers
Junior Road Safety Officers
Each year the school as a small group of pupils from across Key Stage Two who are elected as Junior Road Safety Officers (JRSO's). Their role involves raising awareness of hw to keep safe on the roads and pavements.
Regular meetings are held to voice concerns, discuss road safety and how the importance of this can be communicated to keep everyone safe. The team lead assemblies on Road Safety, run competitions to raise awareness and monitor traffic and parking outside the school.
Our JRSO’s remind our pupils to walk, cycle, scooter or park and stride to school and track their journey on Travel Tracker to gain their WOW badges. They also remind our pupils to Be Bright Be Seen, in our latest campaign.
